overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding a 5:00 p.m. October 1 executive session on topics outside any statutory purpose and by failing to periodically review executive session minutes; the 6:00 p.m. session was proper, and two related allegations were not reached.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board entered executive session on October 1 (5:00 p.m. session) without a proper statutory purpose.
allegations.key_passage: However, we find that the topics discussed during the 5:00 p.m. executive session did not fit within Purpose 1, or any other of the ten executive session purposes permitted by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 1 6:00 p.m. executive session also lacked a proper purpose; the AG found it was properly held under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the 6:00 p.m. executive session was properly held under Purpose 1, and that the Board may continue to withhold the 6:00 p.m. executive session minutes from public disclosure at this time.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice for the 5:00 p.m. October 1 executive session did not give enough detail about the anticipated topic.
allegations.key_passage: we do not determine whether the meeting notice was sufficiently detailed, as the discussion should not have taken place in executive session at all.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board should have released the October 1 5:00 p.m. executive session minutes sooner than November 23.
allegations.key_passage: we do not determine when the purpose for that session expired, as it was not proper to begin with.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to periodically review its executive session minutes for possible release to the public.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review all executive session meeting minutes at reasonable intervals.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (ordered).
Within 60 days of receipt of the determination, review all outstanding executive session minutes to determine whether continued non-disclosure is warranted (ordered).
remedy_passage: We also order the Board, within 60 days of receipt of this determination, to review all outstanding executive session minutes in order to determine whether continued non-disclosure is warranted.
